documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI)
documents.summary: The Provost page gives general guidelines for generative AI use (accuracy, confidential data, phishing, procurement), definitions, and FAQs for faculty, staff and students. It sets no AI rule for coursework: students are told to follow each instructor's policy and ask when unsure, and faculty are told to state expectations in the syllabus.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no stance of its own: students are told "Different fields, courses, and instructors will have different policies and guidelines for how AI can or cannot be used", and faculty are told to "be clear about expectations for student use of AI". The decision is handed to instructors, so delegates.

units.why: The passage lists open questions ('What impact will generative AI have on our ability to measure student learning') that frame why the university is issuing guidance; nearest is the institutional preamble P56, but it lists unanswered questions, not principles.
units.anchor: What impact will generative AI have on our ability to measure student learning
units.policy: The university frames its guidance around open questions about measuring student learning and research integrity.
units.fit_note: States open questions the university has not answered rather than purpose, scope or principles.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded the open question 'What impact will generative AI have on our ability to measure student learning and maintain research security and integrity?'. It is a distinct framing statement in the source, kept as informs. B's fit note (states open questions rather than purpose, scope or principles) is kept.

units.why: The page lists open concerns, "ethics and bias, business processes and efficiencies", as impacts of AI; it states worries, not a rule, so informs. P53 fits best because it names ethics and bias, but it also names learning and workforce, which P53 does not capture.
units.anchor: raising questions about student learning and assessment, ethics and bias
units.fit_note: Also names student learning, assessment, workforce and new opportunities, not only ethics and bias.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded 'raising questions about student learning and assessment, ethics and bias' (P53). Coder B coded a different sentence (the 'What impact will generative AI have on our ability to measure student learning' question). Both are separate rationale statements, so both are kept.
